title: Choosing Polynomial Perturbation Subsets
summary: Perturbing a polynomial function can yield a non-polynomial one, but choosing the modified subset to avoid polynomial closeness while retaining practicality remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Given a polynomial function $P$ over $\mathbb{Z}_{p^n}$, determine how to choose a subset of $\mathbb{Z}_{p^n}$ on which to modify $P$ so that the resulting function $F$ is non-polynomial, is not too close to a polynomial function, and remains practical to implement. The unresolved tradeoff is that perturbing too small a subset leaves $F$ too close to being polynomial, whereas perturbing a large subset may make $F$ expensive to implement.

scope.domain: Design of non-polynomial S-box components over integer rings by perturbing polynomial functions.
parameters: Perturbation subset: specifies where $P$ is modified, with its size affecting polynomial closeness and implementation cost
scope.unresolved_remainder: Choose the perturbation subset so that the resulting function is non-polynomial, not too close to a polynomial function, and practical to implement.

citations.label: The ABC of Symmetric Primitives over Integer Rings: Milk Before Meat

progress.summary: The source notes that perturbing a polynomial function on a subset can produce a non-polynomial function and explicitly poses subset selection as a problem. It identifies the tradeoff between small-subset polynomial closeness and large-subset implementation cost without resolving it.
